title: Discussion on multi-GPU support for cuFFT and cuSOLVER
body_excerpt: Original context: See #2644.  Some of CUDA libraries like cuFFT and cuSOLVER provide native multi-GPU support. However, there is no guarantee that multiple GPUs will outperform single GPU; on the contrary, for cuFFT I found in https://github.com/cupy/cupy/pull/2644#issuecomment-558835428 that any workload that can be handled in one GPU should ***not*** be processed using multi GPUs; the extra data transfer just kills the performance (even if NVLinks are present). I suspect the same holds for cuSOLVER.  Since CuPy operations incurs additional memory overhead, I think it is clear that multi-GPU is useful only when the workload is too large to fit in one GPU. title: Runtime integer calculation overflow
body_excerpt: Not sure if this can be classified as a bug but I thought I would post this just incase it isn't known about. Values known at compile time, and are thus computed in Python, use Python's long int and can represent values outside the range of a normal integer so you can get results that don't quite match.  ``` from numba import cuda import numpy as np  @cuda.jit def test_kernel(a,b,c,test): 	i = cuda.grid(1)  	test[0] = a**b%c 	test[1] = 11**19%1009  a, b, c = 11, 19, 1009 test = cuda.device_array(2, dtype = np.uint32)  test_kernel[1, 1](a,b,c,test)  print(a**b%c,test.copy_to_host()) >>> 902 [759 902] ```
